# Local CI Gate: Rollout and Rollback Runbook (TRD-010)

For a repository adopting the gate. The planning logic lives in
`local-ci-rollout.js` and is reached through the gate CLI's `rollout`
subcommand (`local-ci-cli.js rollout`), so it works from a checkout, a plugin
install or the Pi bundle. Locate the CLI exactly as the gate skill does
(`tool-path-resolution`); never hard-code a repo path. Send one JSON payload on
stdin: `{"action": "<name>", "input": {...}}` with `action` one of `snapshot`,
`plan-enable`, `plan-rollback`, `preconditions`. It only snapshots,
plans and checks; it never calls GitHub. A person with the rights named in
[Owner approvals](#owner-approvals) runs each call. The function names used
below (`snapshotProtection`, `planEnable`, ...) are what each action runs.

## Owner approvals

Each protection-changing step needs an admin of the adopting repository. The
list below is `OWNER_APPROVALS` in the library; a test checks every
protection-changing plan step is on it.

| Step | Approver | Needs approval | What is approved |
|---|---|---|---|
| `snapshot` | repository admin | no | read-only GET of the current protection |
| `first-success-status` | repository owner | yes | publishing the first real local-ci success, with the maintainer's own `gh` login, on a current head commit |
| `enable-protection` | repository admin | yes | local-ci check required by name, unpinned; hosted checks no longer required |
| `rollback-protection` | repository admin | yes | restoring the snapshot; hosted checks required again |

## Enable

Run in order; stop at the first refusal.

1. **Snapshot** (`snapshot`). Read the current protection and record it with
   `snapshotProtection(response, {repo, branch, now})`, then store the result
   somewhere durable (a file in the repo's ops notes, not a secret store; it
   holds no credential):
   `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/branches/BRANCH/protection`.
   A malformed or partial response is refused, never snapshotted as a guess.
   The snapshot keeps `required_status_checks` (with `strict` and each check's
   `app_id`), `enforce_admins.enabled`, `required_pull_request_reviews`,
   `restrictions`, the repo, branch and timestamp.
2. **Preconditions.** `checkEnablementPreconditions({repoRoot, hasReportedSuccess})`
   must return `ok: true`. It refuses when any of these fails (all reasons listed):
   - the measurement note `MEASUREMENT.md` is missing, unfilled or `unmeasured` (TRD-013);
   - the local status context has not yet reported success on this repository;
   - `BASELINE.md` is missing.
3. **First real success status** (`first-success-status`). GitHub only allows a
   check to be required if it completed successfully in that repository within
   the past seven days. So, before touching protection, run the gate for a
   current head commit of the protected branch's PRs (`gate` mode of this skill)
   and let it post a real success with the maintainer's own `gh` login. Then set
   `hasReportedSuccess: true` for the step-2 check. Never post a status by hand.
4. **Enable protection** (`enable-protection`).
   `planEnable({snapshot, statusContext, replaces})` returns the calls as data.
   `statusContext` is `status_context` from `.ensemble/local-ci.yaml`; the check
   is added unpinned (`app_id: null`, written as `-1`).
   `replaces` is the list of currently required check names that the local gate
   covers (for this repository `validate`, `test (22)`, `test (24)`: the job
   names in the approval set, with ` (<node>)` for matrix entries). Only those
   are removed. Every other required check (a secret scan, a deploy preview)
   stays required, because the gate does not run it; the plan lists them under
   `keeps`. A name in `replaces` that is not currently required is refused, so a
   typo cannot leave a hosted check in place while enablement looks done.
   The one protection-changing call is
   `PATCH /repos/OWNER/REPO/branches/BRANCH/protection/required_status_checks`
   with body `{"strict": <snapshot strict>, "checks": [<kept checks with their app_id>, {"context": "<statusContext>", "app_id": -1}]}`.
   It replaces the list of required checks only, so `enforce_admins`, reviews and
   restrictions are untouched and `strict` is carried over.
   The `PUT .../protection` endpoint is deliberately not used: it replaces the
   whole protection and would drop anything the snapshot missed.
   **Before this step, remove `hosted_reuse`** from `.ensemble/local-ci.yaml` (see
   [Hosted reuse](#hosted-reuse-skip-a-local-run-that-hosted-ci-already-did)), or
   always pass `forceLocal: true` to `gate`. A head accepted through hosted jobs
   never gets an `ensemble/local-ci` status, so with that check required GitHub
   would block a merge the CLI called ready.
5. **Owner approval, apply, read back.** The repository admin reviews the plan
   and approves `enable-protection` (see [Owner approvals](#owner-approvals)),
   then applies the `PATCH`. Run the plan's read-only `GET .../protection` and
   confirm the local check is listed (reported with `app_id: null`), the hosted
   checks it replaced are gone, and everything else matches the snapshot.

## Trust model

The required check is **unpinned**: it is required by name, with no GitHub App
behind it (`app_id` is `null` when read and is written to GitHub as `-1`,
GitHub's documented "any app" value). The gate posts the status with the
maintainer's own `gh` login. Any identity with write access to the repository
can post a status under that name. `pr-merge` accepts one whose run record
verifies (head-SHA binding, runner blob hash, workflow-set hash, log digest,
review state); it does not verify who posted it. The gate therefore prevents
accidents and unverified agent merges. It does not stop deliberate forgery by
someone with write access. A repository that needs forge-resistance would need
a pinned GitHub App, which is separate future work and is not part of this gate.

## Hosted reuse (skip a local run that hosted CI already did)

When hosted CI has already passed on the PR's exact head, `gate` and `merge` can accept those results instead of repeating the work in a clean clone. The CLI reads them from GitHub itself (the Actions runs and jobs for that head SHA); the skill and the payload never supply them. Design and trust limits: TRD-015 in `docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4dec59b8-local-ci-pr-approval.md`.

**Enable.** Add a `hosted_reuse` block to `.ensemble/local-ci.yaml` on the base branch (it is read from the base ref, so it applies once merged):

```yaml
hosted_reuse:
  covers: [install, scripts-tests, validate, generate-validate, generated-drift, test]   # abbreviated: list EVERY name in `steps` (this repository's file lists all nine)
  extra_workflows:
    - file: .github/workflows/generated-drift.yml
      jobs:
        - id: drift
```

Every step in `steps` MUST be listed in `covers`; if one is missing, reuse is off. `extra_workflows` names hosted jobs outside the default approval set. See the comment in this repository's `.ensemble/local-ci.yaml` for the exact current block.

**Rollout order.** A gate CLI older than this change rejects the unknown config key `hosted_reuse` and then refuses every PR once the key reaches `dev`. Release and update clients first, then merge the config block. The change that added hosted reuse adds the client code and the config block together, so any client not yet updated refuses every PR to `dev` until it is. The gate also needs permission to post commit statuses BEFORE the run (the write-ahead `pending`) as well as after it; without it the gate refuses to run.

**Disable.** Remove the `hosted_reuse` block, or delete one name from `covers` (an uncovered step turns reuse off entirely). Either is a normal reviewed change to the config.

**`forceLocal`.** `gate` accepts `forceLocal: true` (a boolean) in its payload to skip the hosted shortcut and run locally.

**Results.** `check`/`merge` and `gate` report `source:"hosted"` and `hostedJobs` when hosted results were accepted. `gate` then runs nothing and posts no status, so no `ensemble/local-ci` status exists for that head; `merge` accepts it all the same, and a verified local status still takes precedence when both exist. The hosted check happens before the lock (see "One run at a time"): it only reads GitHub, so a `gate` that accepts hosted results never queues behind a running gate, and a refused one then runs locally under the lock like any other.

**A refusal is not a failure.** A reason beginning `hosted CI not accepted:` means a hosted result could not be verified (job missing, still running, red, on another commit, a workflow file that differs from the base's, an underivable job name, GitHub unreachable). `gate` then runs locally exactly as before and reports `hostedRefused`; `merge` refuses and shows the hosted reason beside the local one. Run `gate` (or wait for hosted CI and check again).

**A PR that changes a workflow file.** Hosted CI ran the PR head's own copy of the workflow, so a PR that edits one of the hosted workflow files is refused for reuse and graded by the local gate; the change takes effect after it merges.

**Node 22 gap.** Hosted `validate` and `drift` run on Node 24 only, while the local gate runs 22 and 24; accepting hosted results gives up the Node 22 run of those steps, and `generate-validate` is declared covered by the generate step, which hosted `validate` and `drift` run. This is accepted in the config; delete the name from `covers` to refuse it.

**Not verified.** Who triggered the hosted run, and that the workflow's steps are honest beyond the file being identical to the base's. A `pull_request` run executes on the merge commit of head and base, not the bare head, and that base tip may not be the base tip now (the run's `base.sha` is not compared, because `dev` moves constantly and equality would switch reuse off). External actions (`owner/repo@tag`) are trusted as pinned by tag, not by SHA. The verified SHA is not passed to the merge step (`--match-head-commit`): `pr-merge.yaml` is at its word ceiling. `merge` and `gate` re-read the PR once after hosted verification.

**Runs are bound to this PR.** Only runs whose `pull_requests` list holds this PR's number with the PR's base branch count. A run of another PR sharing the head SHA, of another base branch, or with an empty `pull_requests` (fork-PR runs, a closed PR) is ignored: it cannot count and cannot mask or replace this PR's run. A fork PR therefore never gets hosted acceptance: the gate runs locally.

**Write-ahead.** A non-dry `gate` that is going to run locally posts `pending` in the configured context (description `ci-local running @ <sha8>`) on the exact head BEFORE the run, once it holds the lock. If that post fails (no permission, rate limit, any error), the gate refuses to run (`stage: "pending"`, `error` beginning `cannot record that a local run is starting`, nothing cloned, nothing else posted): it never runs a local run it cannot record. The final post then supersedes the pending: `success` on a pass, `failure` for a head-bound refusal.

**What vetoes hosted acceptance.** After hosted verification succeeds, `merge` and `gate` each read the head's commit statuses from GitHub themselves (`commits/<head>/statuses?per_page=100`); the caller's `statuses` payload no longer decides, except that a `failure`, `error`, `pending` or other non-success status the caller reports in the configured context vetoes when GitHub lists nothing in that context for the head, and one that names no usable commit SHA vetoes always. GitHub lists statuses newest first and the FIRST status in the configured context decides. `success` clears ONLY when its record verifies for this head: `verifyRecord` binds the commit, the trusted config blob, the workflow-set hash and the record format. It does NOT bind who posted the status, so anyone with write access can post a verifying success (honest-actor model, AC-004-4). `pending`, `failure`, `error`, any other state, an unverified success, an unreadable or malformed list, a full page of 100 without the context, and a list not in newest-first order all veto (fail closed). No status in the context at all means no veto: nothing local ever ran. `merge` then refuses, naming the reason; re-run the gate with `forceLocal: true`. `gate` skips the hosted shortcut, runs locally and reports `hostedRefused`.

**Which local refusals leave what.** HEAD-BOUND refusals publish a `failure` status for the head, which supersedes the pending and vetoes: `step-failed`, `unsupported-step`, `clone-tampered`, `unexpected-output`, `unreadable-workflow`, `clone-moved`, `clone-config-changed`, `runner-error` and any unknown kind. TRANSIENT ones publish nothing and LEAVE THE PENDING in place, so they keep vetoing until a later local run passes (see Clearing a veto): `invalid-input`, `prerequisite`, `secrets`, `cleanup`, `unfetchable-head`, `node-version` (the head was never evaluated; this trades availability for safety, on purpose). A crash, a kill, a timeout, a thrown runner or a failed final post also leaves the pending (a thrown runner is first turned into a head-bound `runner-error` failure and posted; the gate report says `pendingRemains:true` when the final post did not publish). Dry runs and the `run` command never publish, so their outcome never vetoes.

**Stale head note (kata `w6tn`).** The gate grades the PR head; hosted CI grades the merge ref. When a `run` or `gate` report FAILS and the head does not contain the base ref, the report gains `notes: [{kind:"head-behind-base", behind:N, baseRef, message}]`: a failure may then be staleness (typically the pi version-bump hook or generated drift after a main release), so update the branch onto the base and re-run before treating it as a defect. The note is advisory: it never changes `ok`, `mergeReady`, `failures` or the posted status, is absent on a pass or when the head contains the base, and a git error yields no note.

**Clearing a veto.** Any passing local run of `gate` clears one, forced or not: it posts a verified `success`, which is then the latest status. A non-forced `gate` whose hosted check is vetoed falls through to a local run, and if that run passes it posts the verified success; `forceLocal: true` only skips the hosted check. A bare or unverifiable success never clears. `merge`'s local route applies the same rule: a newer `failure`, `pending` or unverified success on GitHub beats an older verified success in the payload; when GitHub lists nothing in the context, the payload's verified success is accepted. The payload's own non-success statuses in the context are judged exactly as on the hosted route, by one shared rule: one that names no usable commit SHA vetoes, one on this head vetoes while GitHub lists nothing in the context (a verified GitHub success supersedes it), and one on another full SHA is ignored. The refusal is the local-route veto (`localFailure`, re-run the gate with `forceLocal: true`), not `hostedRefused`. The veto context is the `status_context` of the BASE config of the PR's base branch (`ensemble/local-ci` in every repository surveyed); a base config that names another context moves the veto with it, because the gate posts to the same configured context.

**Runner cleanup.** The runner no longer throws over a result when a step leaves unreadable directories: permissions are repaired and removal retried. A clone that still cannot be removed is a head-bound `runner-error` failure, even if every step passed, and is published; remove the named directory by hand before re-running. The untracked-file check also fails closed: when git reports that it cannot open a directory (a step made one unreadable), the run is `clone-tampered` ("could not inspect the clone"), so a step cannot hide planted files there.

**Repo-local actions.** Hosted acceptance is refused when a required job of a required base workflow uses a repo-local action or reusable workflow (a `uses:` starting with `./`, at job or step level), because the PR can change those files while the workflow file stays identical.

**More static refusals.** A run bound to this PR with a non-integer id refuses (it is never dropped). Required jobs, and every job in their `needs:` closure, refuse when they use repo-local actions, set `continue-on-error` to anything but `false`, or have an `if:` matching `github\.(head_ref|actor|triggering_actor|event)\b`: that is `github.head_ref`, `github.actor`, `github.triggering_actor`, `github.event` and every `github.event.<anything>`; `github.event_name` is NOT refused (the trigger fixes it, the PR does not control it). These are early static refusals: a blacklist of PR-controlled contexts, NOT a proof. The real guard is the step check below. Still unverified: matrix or env values and reusable workflows from other repos.

**Needed jobs and step conclusions.** Every job in a required job's `needs:` closure must have concluded `success` in the same run (a closure job with a matrix, a computed name or no definition refuses). Every step of each required job must have concluded `success`; the jobs listing's steps are mapped positionally to the base workflow's steps, a skipped step is accepted only where the base step's `if:` is a pure matrix comparison (for example `Upload coverage` on `test (22)`), and GitHub's own `Set up job`, `Complete job` and `Post` steps are exempt. This is the real guard.

**What the PR head's steps run with.** A step is the PR head's own code running as the maintainer, so the runner withholds what it can. Each run creates one scratch directory (mode 0700) and points `HOME`, `GH_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME` and `TMPDIR` into it, sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` to the null device, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1` and `GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1`, and adds a fresh `ENSEMBLE_LOCAL_CI_RUN` id. Besides those, a step gets only an allowlist (`USER`, `LOGNAME`, `SHELL`, `LANG`, `LC_ALL`, `TERM`, `NODE_OPTIONS`), `CI=true`, `npm_config_cache` and the secrets the config names; `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, the enterprise and GitLab tokens, `NPM_TOKEN`, `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `GIT_ASKPASS`, `SSH_ASKPASS`, `GH_HOST`, `AWS_*` and every other variable are never forwarded. `PATH` is the runner's bin directory, then a scratch directory holding a stub for the GitHub CLI (prints that the gate does not give the PR head's code its GitHub credential, exits 127), then the maintainer's `PATH` unchanged: the toolchain stays reachable, and dropping entries would gain nothing because an absolute path still works. After the last step, before the clone is removed and before the gate posts its final status, the runner SIGKILLs the process group of every step process that still had a member and every process of the current user whose environment carries the run's marker (Linux: `/proc/<pid>/environ`; macOS: `ps -axww -E`, which does not show the environment of Apple's own binaries such as `/bin/sh`, `/bin/sleep` or `/usr/bin/perl`; other platforms: no sweep), never its own pid or its parent, and reports `leftoverProcessesKilled` when it killed any, which is not a failure. A daemon started by one step keeps running for the later steps of the same run. The runner's own git, clone and fetch commands keep the maintainer's environment.

**Residuals.** A status writer with the gate's credentials can post a verifying success and so clear a veto, and so can the PR head's own steps, which run as the maintainer. The isolation above closes the easy routes: inherited tokens and `GH_*`/`XDG_*`/`HOME`, git global and system config, a bare call of the GitHub CLI, and leftover process groups and marker-carrying processes at the end of the run. It does NOT close what head code running as the same OS user can still reach: the real credential files by absolute path or through `os.userInfo().homedir`, the macOS keychain (`security`, `git-credential-osxkeychain`), any other credential store the maintainer holds, a child that scrubs its environment AND leaves the process group (on macOS also one that left the group under an Apple binary, whose environment the sweep cannot read), and a workflow that holds `statuses: write`. HOME redirection is not a sandbox. Not done, as options: `sandbox-exec` on macOS, `bwrap` or `unshare` on Linux, steps under another OS user or in a container, or a status-posting identity the steps can never reach. `verifyRecord` binds the commit, the config blob, the workflow-set hash and the record format, not the creator, and the local success route has the same property, so hosted reuse is no weaker than what the gate already trusts. Also open: the window between the statuses read and the actual merge (TOCTOU); a dead gate leaves `pending`, and the precheck does not start a gate while any status in the context exists, so recovery is a manual `gate` run; a veto is bound to one head SHA, so a new commit, even with an identical tree, is a new head with no local record that hosted CI alone grades unless the gate runs on it; a dry run or the `run` command records nothing, so nothing it finds vetoes; expressions outside the whitelist are refused rather than evaluated; steps inside composite actions are not listed by the API and the name mapping is positional; external actions are pinned by tag; `base.sha` is not compared.

**A head that moves.** After hosted verification succeeds, `merge` and `gate` re-read the PR and refuse if it is no longer open or its head changed; `gate` then stops at stage `config` and does not fall back to a local run.

**Branch protection.** Never change branch protection from this skill, from the CLI or from any command. Since 2026-11-06 protection on `dev` requires the hosted checks `validate`, `test (22)` and `test (24)` (see Rollback), so GitHub itself waits for hosted CI. With reuse enabled, the gate verdict (`merge`) no longer needs a local gate run once those jobs are green on the head; it still refuses when they are not, and a PR whose workflow files changed is graded by the local gate. Pointing protection back at `ensemble/local-ci` stays a separate owner-approved step (see Enable, which requires removing `hosted_reuse` or always passing `forceLocal: true` first).

## A PR branch that is behind its base is refused

The gate reads its configuration from the PR's **base** branch and compares the PR head's workflows with it. A PR whose
branch was cut before the base last changed a required workflow is therefore refused, not skipped: it reports
`unsupported-step` for every workflow step the base's configuration does not mirror, and posts nothing. This was seen on
the first real run against an open PR (a branch 116 commits behind `dev`, whose `test.yml` still had Python steps that
`dev` had since removed). The refusal is correct: the head's workflows are not the ones the gate was configured for.

What to do: have the PR author update the branch from the base (merge or rebase) and re-run. The operator should not
edit another author's branch. A refusal like this is not evidence the gate is broken, and it is not a reason to loosen
`.ensemble/local-ci.yaml`.

## Rollback

1. `planRollback({snapshot})` using the stored snapshot returns one
   protection-changing call (`rollback-protection`):
   `PATCH /repos/OWNER/REPO/branches/BRANCH/protection/required_status_checks`
   with the snapshot's `strict` and its original checks, each with its original
   `app_id` (an any-app check, recorded as `null`, is written back as `-1`).
   The hosted checks are required again and the local status is no longer required.
   Applying `planEnable` then `planRollback` to a protection store restores a
   protection equal to the snapshot (covered by a test against an in-memory store).
2. Run the plan's `GET` and compare it with the snapshot.
3. **`pr-merge` and bot reviews.** `pr-merge` classifies reviewers by account
   type; a bot's CHANGES_REQUESTED review and unresolved bot threads do not block
   its merge decision, and rolling back protection does not change that. What
   rolling back changes is the merge gate: GitHub itself again requires the
   hosted checks, so a PR without hosted CI success cannot merge even if the
   local gate passed. If `pr-merge` should also stop merging on the local status
   (so it waits for hosted CI again), revert the commit that changed
   `packages/git/commands/pr-merge.yaml` to merge on the gate verdict and
   regenerate; that is a separate, reviewed change.

## Optional pre-PR gate step (fix-issue, implement-trd-beads)

`fix-issue` and `implement-trd-beads` are unchanged. A caller that wants the PR
to open already approved runs, after the final commit and push of the branch and
before opening the PR: resolve the branch head SHA (full 40 hex), run the gate for
that head (`MODE=gate`, this skill), confirm `posted:true` and `mergeReady:true`,
then open the PR. The status is attached to the commit, so the PR's head carries
it from the moment it opens. If any commit is added afterwards the head moves and
the gate must run again; a status on an older commit never counts.

## One run at a time (lock, queue, capacity, load policy)

`gate` and `run` take a lock around the run step (`lib/local-ci-lock.js`): both clone the head and run the repository's
whole CI, so both queue. The lock is a PID lockfile at `~/.ensemble/locks/local-ci-gate.lock`: outside every worktree and
persistent (never `/tmp`). It lives under the user's home directory, so it serializes the processes that share that home;
another account, or a process started with a different `$HOME`, has its own lock. A holder whose pid is dead (or whose
record is unreadable) is reclaimed; a live holder is honoured; a lock written by another host cannot be judged and is
honoured. A second run waits its turn, polling (waiters are not served first-come-first-served), and the report carries
`queued_ms`. Posting the status happens after the lock is released, and the lock is released when the run throws. The
review precheck (`review-precheck-cli.js`) starts a detached `gate` per head; that gate takes the lock like any other,
and while it waits its start marker stays live, so a second precheck for the same head starts nothing.

A run that cannot get the lock stops at `stage:"lock"` with an `errorCode` and runs and posts nothing: `lock-timeout` (the
wait ran out; the error names the holder pid, or the lock path when it holds no readable record, such as a dangling
symlink), `load-too-high`, `bad-lock-policy`, or `lock-io` (the lock directory cannot be created, or the lock cannot be
linked or read; the error names the path and the cause). If a holder's pid is gone but its number was reused by an
unrelated process, or the path is a dangling symlink, remove the file by hand after checking: the gate never deletes a
lock held by a live pid or one it cannot read.

Policy comes from the maintainer's environment (the payload cannot carry it; a malformed value refuses the run with
`errorCode` `bad-lock-policy`):

| Variable | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `ENSEMBLE_LOCAL_CI_LOCK_DIR` | directory holding the lock file | `~/.ensemble/locks` |
| `ENSEMBLE_LOCAL_CI_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` | longest wait for the lock (`0` = try once) | `1800000`, or one worst-case hold if longer |
| `ENSEMBLE_LOCAL_CI_MAX_LOAD` | 1-minute load-average ceiling; unset = no load check | unset |
| `ENSEMBLE_LOCAL_CI_LOAD_POLICY` | above the ceiling: `wait` (until the timeout) or `refuse` (`errorCode` `load-too-high`) | `wait` |

### Capacity

A waiter waits as long as the runs ahead of it take. One gate on this repository takes about 5 to 6 minutes on a quiet
machine (`MEASUREMENT.md`: 334 s cold, 304 s warm) and 8 to 9 under load (plan, section 1). The floor of 30 minutes
covers three runs ahead of yours at 9 minutes each, the three-swarm case the lock exists for; that is the supported queue
depth at normal durations.

The runner has no run-level deadline. Every command it starts (the Node version check of each required Node version,
then each trusted step) is cut off after 10 minutes, and nothing else is bounded, so one run takes at worst
`Node versions × (steps + 1) × 10 minutes`, plus the clone and the Node download, which have no timeout. For this
repository's `.ensemble/local-ci.yaml` (2 Node versions, 9 steps) that is 200 minutes. A run asks for the lock with that
figure for its own config, and the default wait is raised to it when it is longer than 30 minutes, so one holder that
stays inside the runner's limits can never make a waiter give up. At that worst case the supported depth is one run
ahead of yours. An explicit `ENSEMBLE_LOCAL_CI_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` always wins: for a deeper queue raise it to the number of
runs ahead of yours times the duration you see, plus a margin; lower it to find a stuck lock sooner (a pid-reuse lock is
refused only when the wait runs out).

### Known gaps

- A dead holder whose pid was reused by an unrelated live process stays "held" until the wait runs out.
- A gate killed with SIGKILL leaves the CI step it was running alive: the runner starts every step in its own process
  group, so killing the gate's group does not reach it, and the lock sees only the dead pid. The next run can start while
  that step is still going. After killing a gate, look for its leftover step and stop that too.
- A run that waits for the lock keeps the head it was started for. If the PR head moves meanwhile it still runs and
  attests the old head, which never counts for the new one (statuses are per commit).

Do not start gates (or `run`) during a reviewer swarm. The lock keeps runs from overlapping each other; it does not know
about reviewer or verifier agents, so the caller sequences those: run the gate before they are dispatched or after they
finish.
